title: Is it ethical to make a game using ai?
author: Random_F0XY
selftext: Ive tried for years to learn how to code. I can't learn no matter what I do I've tried online courses in-person courses and YouTube videos. I just can't code my own things. I've also tried to learn blender and Unity to make my games but I also don't understand those. I just got open ai go recently and I can debug somewhat and I don't have any other way to make it. I'm afraid people won't want it because it's ai made, which I understand and I'm also conflicted cause on one hand the companies who make ai are terrible and hate them but i really want to see this game through

comments.author: TemporalBias
comments.body: It sounds like you might be interested in open weight and local AI models that could help you to get you away from the AI providers. Applications like LM Studio and Jan make running local models relatively painless.

replies.author: InsolentCoolRadio
replies.body:
To get a wide depth and breadth feedback quickly

It can also help you break down your ideas into smaller chunks and work on the root of each issue one thing at a time

As it relates to your title question about whether or not it’s ethical to make games with AI, it can help you with better framing the question, like by starting with your own moral framework (for example: a Baptist Preacher and a Rothbardian Mercenary are operating on very different ethical principles). There’s also the question of premises in question (what set of facts are you using, how valid are they, are there important things you’re missing, etc.)

After doing that, you’ll have a more clear idea of what you find confusing (or more likely resolve your contradictions in the process) and form a more direct question that’s more likely to get you the answers you’re looking for

It can also provide you with emotional, infrastructural, and technical support for your project

comments.author: Edenisb
comments.body:
Ethics are a weird thing and they are personal, for me my take is when I am at a restaurant and im eating some really amazing spaghetti and it tastes great, I really don't care how that pasta was made, it just takes good.

But some people hate ai and think its ruining the world, so just make something for yourself and if other people want to try it sub like this have people that might find fun in it.

And if its REALLY fun more people won't care than the people who do, haters tend to be the loudest and right now its super cool for people to hate ai for virtue signaling.

comments.author: Candid-Remote2395
comments.body: A lot of that concern is performative. AI made games are far from unethical compared to half the stuff we use daily. These are the same people who will buy clothes made in sweatshops and meat from factory farms.

comments.author: Kaelzoroden
comments.body: I'd worry less about the ethics and more about the logistics. If you don't know how to use something like Blender or Unity, then you're going to have a very difficult time getting good results out of AI. In many ways, AI is a force multiplier—it increases your output by orders of magnitude, but if you don't know what you're fundamentally doing, all it ends up doing is producing polished turds in record time.

comments.author: TechgeekOne
comments.body:
As long as you make the effort to build a the game you want I don't see any reason why you should care what other people think. Go build your game.

Also pretty much every single thing you use every day is  created by companies participating in some pretty heinous practices or has done so in the past. This is just the newest and particularly public batch of companies. Maybe they survive, maybe they don't, you're not really taking a moral stance using the technologies available to you (an frankly anyone claiming otherwise is a massive hypocrite). If that idea bothers you there's always open weight models too.

comments.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
comments.body: Making a game with AI is no different than learning to code, you have to do it regardless of whether people will like it or not. Once you accept that the rest will start to fall in place.

comments.author: HomeTimeLegend
comments.body:
You said you've tried but don't understand unity or blender might imply you're gonna struggle. The AI will make mistakes and you will have to know or quickly figure out how things fit together to get far without breaking things. you could stumble into getting a simple fun game goin without knowing a thing but it depends on the ideas.   
  
It's the best time ever to try, saying that, It'll get easier in the future if you find it too difficult now, always does. 

Writing code is generally tedious, whether you know the language well or not... at least I've always felt that way. I love the change. 

If it's simply a case of you feel bad for trying AI cause of other people I wouldn't worry about it, the stance can't last and anyone complaining about energy consumption or water usage is online, accessing data centers constantly for the social media or whatever services they use. It's all hipocrasy.
